title: The tail's sequence picks the partner

scenes.tts: The two kinases are on. They add phosphate to tyrosines outside the kinase core, mostly on the two flexible tails. Each of those phosphates is a docking site. So how does a tail pick its partner?
scenes.visual: Two switched-on kinases under the membrane; phosphate badges fly onto tyrosines along their tails; one is labelled docking site; grey question marks appear.
scenes.narration: The two kinases are on. They add phosphate to tyrosines outside the kinase core, mostly on the two flexible tails. Each of those phosphates is a docking site. So how does a tail pick its partner?

scenes.tts: An S H 2 domain binds a phosphotyrosine. It also checks the few residues that follow. So the sequence decides which protein binds. On the E G F receptor tail, phosphotyrosine ten sixty-eight has an asparagine two residues later. That suits the S H 2 domain of Grb two, which leads to Ras and the MAP kinase cascade. Phosphotyrosine nine ninety-two, on the same tail, binds P L C gamma. That enzyme makes I P 3 and D A G.
scenes.caption: An SH2 domain binds a phosphotyrosine. It also checks the few residues that follow. So the sequence decides which protein binds. On the EGF receptor tail, phosphotyrosine 1068 has an asparagine two residues later. That suits the SH2 domain of Grb2, which leads to Ras and the MAP kinase cascade. Phosphotyrosine 992, on the same tail, binds PLC-gamma. That enzyme makes IP3 and DAG.
scenes.visual: A tail strip with two sites. A cup-shaped SH2 domain lowers onto phosphotyrosine 1068 and reads the asparagine; it becomes Grb2 with Ras and MAP kinase below. A second cup docks at site 992 and PLC-gamma gives IP3 and DAG.
scenes.narration: An SH2 domain binds a phosphotyrosine. It also checks the few residues that follow. So the sequence decides which protein binds. On the EGF receptor tail, phosphotyrosine 1068 has an asparagine two residues later. That suits the SH2 domain of Grb2, which leads to Ras and the MAP kinase cascade. Phosphotyrosine 992, on the same tail, binds PLC-gamma. That enzyme makes IP3 and DAG.

scenes.tts: Now look at HER three. Its tail has six tyrosines, and each has a methionine three residues later. That suits the S H 2 domains of P I 3 kinase, which leads to Akt. So one activated pair starts several pathways at once. The choice of partner changes the mix.
scenes.caption: Now look at HER3. Its tail has six tyrosines, and each has a methionine three residues later. That suits the SH2 domains of PI 3-kinase, which leads to Akt. So one activated pair starts several pathways at once. The choice of partner changes the mix.
scenes.visual: HER3 tail with six phosphotyrosines; one enlarged motif with a methionine three along; a PI 3-kinase cup docks, leading to Akt. Then three partner-to-pathway rows appear together.
scenes.narration: Now look at HER3. Its tail has six tyrosines, and each has a methionine three residues later. That suits the SH2 domains of PI 3-kinase, which leads to Akt. So one activated pair starts several pathways at once. The choice of partner changes the mix.

scenes.tts: Does each site serve its own protein? The P D G F receptor carries sites for all three proteins on a single chain. Researchers tested the sites one at a time. They changed a tyrosine to phenylalanine, which cannot be phosphorylated. That protein failed to dock, and the others still did. P I 3 kinase uses two such tyrosines.
scenes.caption: Does each site serve its own protein? The PDGF receptor carries sites for all three proteins on a single chain. Researchers tested the sites one at a time. scenes.visual: One PDGF receptor chain with colour-coded sites joined to Grb2, PLC-gamma and PI 3-kinase. One tyrosine becomes phenylalanine; that partner loses its link while the others stay docked. Then the two PI 3-kinase sites pulse.
